clips.send: The European Coal and Steel Community. 1951–1952. France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg pooled their coal and steel — the materials for weapons. French minister Robert Schuman wanted to make war between France and Germany “not merely unthinkable, but materially impossible.”. It grew into the European Economic Community (1958) and the European Union (1993).

clips.send: The Treaty of Rome: a common market. 1957 (in force 1958). The six created the European Economic Community: no tariffs between members and one tariff for goods from outside. Trade among them grew fast; more countries joined in 1973, 1981, 1986 and 1995.

clips.send: One ship blocks world trade. March 2021. The giant container ship Ever Given, about 400 m (1,300 ft) long, got stuck across Egypt’s Suez Canal for six days. Hundreds of ships waited; roughly 12 percent of world trade passes through the canal (approx.). It showed how tightly connected — and fragile — global supply chains are.

clips.send: The United Nations is founded. San Francisco, June 1945, in force 24 Oct 1945. 50 countries signed the UN Charter in San Francisco; China’s delegation signed first, as the first country to fight the Axis. Goals: keep world peace, develop friendly relations among nations, and cooperate on economic, social and human-rights problems. 24 October is United Nations Day. Its headquarters is in New York.

clips.send: 联合国成立。1945年6月旧金山 · 10月24日生效。50个国家在旧金山签署《联合国宪章》，中国代表团第一个签字——中国是最早抗击法西斯侵略的国家。宗旨：维护国际和平与安全，发展各国间的友好关系，合作解决经济、社会和人权等国际问题。10月24日是联合国日。联合国总部设在纽约。
